en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-gurūttara-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi Kingdom during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Anāthapiṇḍada Park.
In the Grove.
At that time, the Venerable Lohitya Kaṅkī was staying in a forest cave at Sāketa.

Then, the Venerable Lohitya Kaṅkī rose early in the morning; having emerged from the cave, he spread out a rope bed on the open ground, laid down his sitting mat (niṣīdana), and sat down cross-legged.

Then a deity of exquisite form and color, having passed the night, approached the Venerable Lohitya. Upon arrival, he paid homage at the feet of the Venerable Lohitya and stood to one side; by the light of that deity, the cave was entirely illuminated with a wondrous radiance.
Having stepped aside to one side, that deva addressed the Venerable Lohityaka, saying:
"Bhikkhu, bhikkhu! Do you hold the 'Verses on the Worthy and Good' (Sujāta-gāthā) and understand their meaning?"
When he had spoken thus, the Venerable Lohityaka replied to that deva:
"O deva, I do not hold the Verses on the Virtuous or their explanation of the meaning."
“O Deva! Do you hold these virtuous verses and understand their meaning?
When he had spoken thus, that deva replied to the Venerable Lohityaka:
“O Bhikṣu! I recite this ‘Verse on the Virtuous,’ yet I do not understand its meaning. “How so, O Deva?”
"Do you uphold the Verses on the Virtuous and Good (Kalyāṇa-sutta) yet not understand their meaning? "O Bhikkhu!
Once, when the Blessed One was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove of the Kalandakas, he spoke these Verses on the Virtuous and Good to the bhikkhus: [the verses follow]."
"One should not recollect the past, nor seek thoughts regarding the future;
the past has already perished and ceased, and the future is unobtainable.
As for the phenomena of the present, one should contemplate each and every one of them."
What is contemplated is not firm; the wise are able to awaken to this themselves.
Having attained it, they are able to proceed further; what wise person would grieve over the end of life?
My mind does not depart from this; even a great multitude cannot liberate me from it.
"Thus one should dwell with firm steadfastness, not abandoning it day or night.
Therefore, regarding these verses of the virtuous and good, people should contemplate them in this way. Thus, monks!
“I uphold the *Kalyāṇamitra-gāthā*, yet I do not understand its meaning. “How so, O Deva?
Who upholds both the *Kalyāṇamitra-gāthā* and its meaning?”
"O bhikṣu! The Blessed One is staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. He has upheld these excellent verses and their meaning; therefore, O bhikṣu!"
You should receive and uphold from the Blessed One these verses on the virtuous and the good, along with their meaning; reflect upon them well, keep them in mind, recite them, and master them.
Why is this so, O bhikṣu?

Those verses of the Worthy and Good, as well as their meaning, are the true meaning and the true Dharma; they lead to the practice of the holy life, the accomplishment of supernormal powers, the supreme path, and are in accordance with Nirvāṇa.

This son of good family, who has faith and delight in training in the Path, and faith and delight in going forth from home to train in the Path, should uphold these virtuous verses and their meaning; he should contemplate them well and mindfully, and he should respectfully maintain them.
When that deva had finished speaking, he prostrated at the feet of the Venerable Lohityāgaṅgi, circumambulated the Venerable Lohityāgaṅgi, and then suddenly vanished from that spot.
Thereupon, not long after that deity had returned, the Venerable Lohityaka spent the rains retreat at Śāketa.

When the three months of the retreat had passed, he had finished making his robes; then, taking his robe and bowl, he set out for Śrāvastī. Traveling by stages, he arrived at Śrāvastī and stayed at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
Thereupon, the Venerable Lohitya approached the Blessed One; having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
Once the Venerable Lohitya was seated to one side, he addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"O Blessed One!..."
At one time, I was staying in the Śiśumāra-guhā, the Cave of the Silent One.
World-Honored One, at dawn,
having risen and emerged from the cave, I prepared a rope seat in the open air, spread out a *niṣīdana*, and sat down cross-legged.

At that time, there was a deva of exquisite form and appearance who, after the night had passed, came to where I was. Having arrived, he prostrated at my feet and stood to one side; by the radiance of that deva, the cave was entirely illuminated with wondrous light.
Having stepped aside to one side, that deva said to me:
"Bhikkhu, bhikkhu! Do you hold the 'Verses on the Virtuous' (Kalyāṇī-gāthā) and their meaning?"
When he had spoken thus, I replied to that deva: "O Deva,
I do not possess these verses on the virtuous and their meaning."
"O Deva! Do you uphold the 'Verses on the Virtuous' and their meaning?
When he had spoken thus, that deva replied to me, saying:
"O Bhikṣu! I have memorized this verse of the virtuous and good, yet I do not understand its meaning. "How so, O Deva?"
“Do you uphold the *Kalyāṇa-sutta* yet fail to understand its meaning? “O Bhikkhu!

Once, when the Blessed One was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove of the Kalandakas, he recited the *Kalyāṇa-sutta* for the bhikkhus without explaining its meaning. Since this sutta was recited as above, I shall not transcribe it again.”
"Thus it is, bhikṣu!
I have held this 'Verses on the Virtuous' (Kalyāṇa-sutta) but do not understand its meaning. "How so, deva?"
"Who is it that upholds these verses on the virtuous and their meaning?
"It is this bhikkhu! The Blessed One is staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park; he is the one who upholds these verses on the virtuous and their meaning."

Therefore, O bhikṣus! You should receive and uphold these virtuous verses and their meaning from the World-Honored One; you should contemplate and keep them in mind, and you should practice them accordingly.
Why is this? O bhikṣu!

Those verses of the virtuous and their meaning are the true meaning; they constitute the practice of the holy life, the accomplishment of supernormal powers, the attainment of the equal path, and are in accord with nirvāṇa.

This son of good family, who with faith and joy seeks the path, who with faith and joy has gone forth from home to study the path, should uphold these noble and virtuous verses along with their meaning; he should contemplate them well and mindfully, and should respectfully maintain them.
When that deva had finished speaking, he prostrated at my feet, circumambulated me, and vanished on the spot. "O Aññā-Koṇḍañña!
Do you know the name of that deva?"
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
I do not know the name of that deva. “This, Śāriputra!”
"He is named the Devaputra Panāmattananda; he is a great general of the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
"Now is the time for the World-Honored One!
Now is the time for the Sugata!"
"May the Blessed One, for the sake of the bhikṣus, speak these auspicious verses and their meaning.
Having heard them from the Blessed One, the bhikṣus shall uphold them."
"Therefore, Kaccāna, listen well and attend closely; I shall speak for you. "So be it, Blessed One."
The Venerable Lohitya-kaṅki received the instruction of the Blessed One.
Since the Blessed One had already spoken these verses as above, they are not written again here: "How is it, Kaṅki?"
“Does a bhikkhu recollect the past?
In this regard, Cāṅkī, if a bhikkhu, regarding past form, delights in it, clings to it, and dwells therein;”
"Past feeling, perception, formations, and past consciousness— if one delights in them, clings to them, or dwells within them—
in this way, Aṅgīrasa,
a bhikkhu recollects the past."
"How is it, Ānanda! How does a bhikkhu not recollect the past?
In this regard, Ānanda!"
Or, a bhikṣu does not delight in, is not attached to, and does not dwell within past form;
he does not delight in, is not attached to, and does not dwell within past feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
In this way, Śāriputra,
a bhikṣu does not dwell on the past. How so, Śāriputra?
"Monks, what should one seek to attend to in the future?
O Kaccāyana, it is that a monk might,
in the future, [be] attracted to form, or delight in it, or become attached to it, and dwell therein."
"Regarding future feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, one finds pleasure therein, becomes attached to them, or dwells within them.
It is in this way, Aṅgīrasa,
that a bhikkhu recollects the future."
"What do you think, Śāriputra!
Might there be a bhikṣu who possesses a thought of seeking nothing in the future?
This, Śāriputra!"
Or, a bhikṣu does not find delight in future form, does not cling to it, and does not dwell within it;
he does not find delight in future feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, does not cling to them, and does not dwell within them.
In this way, Kaccāna,
a bhikkhu should have no thoughts of seeking in the future. How so, Kaccāna?
"Monks, how does one contemplate present phenomena?
Here, Ānanda, a monk delights in present forms; he becomes attached to them and dwells within them."
“Present feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness— within these, one delights,
clings, and dwells. Thus, Aṅgīrasa,
a bhikṣu reflects upon and attends to present phenomena.”
What, O Ānanda, is it that a bhikṣu should not dwell upon with mindfulness in the present? This, O Ānanda,
is what [he should not dwell upon].

Or, a bhikṣu does not find delight in present forms, does not cling to them, and does not dwell upon them; nor does he find delight in present feelings, perceptions, mental formations, or consciousness, nor cling to them, nor dwell upon them; such a bhikṣu does not direct his thoughts toward or dwell upon present phenomena.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
Having heard what the Blessed One had said, the Venerable Lohicca rejoiced and was delighted.
This concludes the Discourse on the Supreme (Uttara-sutta).
